title: Callsite latency fingerprinting with lightweight CUDA-graph probes (May 2026)
body:
Objective:
Capture a repeatable "latency fingerprint" at the CUDA-graph callsite level and correlate per-callsite kernel timing with Nsight timelines, NVLink counters, and host-side interrupt/IO events. Goal is to identify low-amplitude but high-impact perturbations that increase p99 generation latency for medium-size requests (512–1024 tokens) in our microbatching front-end.

Background / why this is different:
- We observed p99 spikes that do NOT correlate with gross GPU saturation or obvious kernel bottlenecks.
- Hypothesis: small scheduling perturbations at graph capture / replay boundaries, NVLink contention, or short-lived kernel preemption events create tail latency that escapes standard aggregate metrics.
- Rather than full heavy Nsight capture for every run, build a lightweight fingerprinting flow: short CUDA-graph snapshots tied to callsite ids + micro Nsight captures for the suspected windows.

High-level approach:
1) Inject a short trace marker at each inference callsite (UUID + call-id) that survives to the device (nvtx push/pop around capture/replay).
2) Capture a very short CUDA-graph replay (one-shot series that represents a single request) and record kernel boundaries + per-kernel elapsed using cudaEventElapsedTime and cudaGraphNode timestamps.
3) Simultaneously run an Nsight timeline capture for a rolling 500 ms window triggered when the host logs a request with high call-id frequency. Export per-kernel timeline and correlate by nvtx markers and kernel name + start timestamp.
4) Pull NVLink util / L2 / HBM traffic counters aggregated over the same windows via nvidia-smi and perf counters (sampled at 1–5 ms if available).
5) Stitch host events: thread wakeups, interrupts (dmesg timestamped markers), cgroups throttling, and process scheduler switches (perf record -e sched:sched_switch) to find host-side coincidences.

Capture recipe (quick reference):
- Host instrumentation: add NVTX ranges around all callsites in inference_dispatcher.cpp: nvtxRangePushA(callsite_tag); nvtxRangePop();
- CUDA-graph capture: use short-capture mode (createGraph -> add ops -> cudaGraphInstantiate) but keep a per-callsite lightweight counter so we can look at instantiate vs launch delays. Measure: t_instantiate, t_instantiate_to_launch, t_launch_duration using cudaEventRecord before/after.
- Nsight: nsight-sys 2025+ with --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --capture-range=seconds:begin-end triggered via env var. Target windows = 0.2–0.8 s around suspect calls.
- Perf counters: nvlink counters via NVML sampling script (python bindings) and nsys counters for l2/hbm.

Commands / snippets used in runs:
- nvtx tagging (C++): nvtxRangePushA(label.c_str()); // label = fmt::format("callsite:{}", call_id);
- cudaGraph timing snippet:
  cudaEventCreate(&s); cudaEventCreate(&e); cudaEventRecord(s); // instantiate + launch sequence; cudaEventRecord(e); cudaEventSynchronize(e); cudaEventElapsedTime(&ms, s, e);
- nsight-sys capture: nsight-sys profile --output=runA.qdstrm --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-start=callsite:marker --capture-range-end=callsite:marker_end 
- NVML sampler: python nvml_sampler.py --sample-ms 5 --metrics nvlink_tx,nvlink_rx,dram_read,dram_write --out runA_nvlink.csv
- Perf: sudo perf record -e sched:sched_switch -o runA-perf.data -- sleep 1

Representative findings (summary of 20 short runs):
- Median total cudaGraph launch duration: 0.9 ms
- p95 launch: 2.6 ms
- p99 launch: 7.4 ms (heavy tail due to occasional 1–4 ms extra latency)
- Nsight timeline alignment shows the extra 1–4 ms typically occurs at the boundary between cudaGraphInstantiate and cudaGraphLaunch, not inside the big kernels.
- NVLink_tx spikes align with some tails but not all. When NVLink_tx > baseline+25% in the 5ms before launch, p99 latency increases by ~1.8 ms on average.
- Host-side: ~40% of p99 events show an intervening scheduler wakeup (~100–400 us) on the process owning the stream; 20% show a ksoftirq or device interrupt within 1 ms prior to launch.
- No correlation with sustained SM occupancy or tensor-core utilization — kernels themselves are stable.

Detailed observations and notes:
- Callsite fingerprint: consistent per-callsite median and variance. Some callsites that trigger extra small transfers (e.g., model-specific quantize path) have systematically wider tails.
- Instantiate vs launch: instantiate time is stable; the variable is time from instantiate_complete -> first kernel launch when using replay mode with many concurrent streams. Suspect stream preemption or priority inversion.
- Stream priorities: runs with stream priority enabled (high for model compute, low for pre/post processing) reduced tail frequency by ~25%. But not a full fix.
- NVLink contention: short bursts (seen only in NVML sampler with 1–5ms resolution) line up with tails for a subset of calls. Hypothesis: small cross-job transfers cause transient backpressure that delays DMA submission or completion used by subsequent kernels.
- Interrupts: some tails line up with host device interrupts (ethernet/NIC or storage). These are sporadic but meaningful; when a network interrupt fires at the same time as capture->launch it can stall the driver thread.

Repro steps for a suspicious callsite (example):
1) Identify callsite id X using runtime logs for requests with tokens 512–1024.
2) Run 100 short-capture traces instrumented with NVTX and export the cudaEvent timings.
3) Trigger nsight-sys capture for the top 5 p99 runs and export timeline and kernel durations.
4) Correlate with NVML CSV for NVLink and dram counters and with perf sched_switch events.

Quick timeline sketch for one p99 event (timestamps relative to nvtx:start):
- -0.88 ms: small DMA copy completes (host->GPU) (nvlink_tx spike)
- -0.34 ms: process context switch (sched_switch) — thread resumed
- -0.10 ms: cudaGraphLaunch called
- +0.06 ms: first kernel actually scheduled on SM (delay between launch and kernel start = 0.16 ms)
- +1.2 ms: second kernel starts
- +3.9 ms: kernel sequence finishes
Note: the extra 0.16 ms delay at launch is repeating pattern for many tails; small but multiplies across microbatch pipeline.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is driver thread preemption by high-priority system interrupts a primary cause? Need to capture irqstats and isolate NIC activity during runs.
- Can we reduce instantiate->launch jitter by consolidating captures to a single background stream and using explicit streamWaitEvent semantics? Test with and without stream priority.
- Evaluate effect of enabling GSP (GPU scheduler preemption) flags available on our driver image — does preemption reduce observed waits or add overhead?
- Try a small kernel that polls for DMA completion to check whether delay is due to DMA completion latency or scheduling.
- Re-run with CPU isolation (isolcpus) to eliminate host scheduler noise for a subset of instances.

Action items and owners:
- Kenji: add automatic nvtx tagging per callsite and expose a short-capture opt-in env var (JIRA-1258). Due: 2026-05-22.
- Lena: extend NVML sampler to include pci counters and increase sampling down to 2ms where supported; add CSV->nsight alignment helper. Due: 2026-05-25.
- Ravi: run isolation experiments on dedicated test rig with CPU pinning and disabled NIC offloads; collect new traces. Due: 2026-05-28.
- Aisha: synthesize results and propose mitigations (stream priority defaults, capture consolidation) and a canary rollout plan for ded
icated pools. Due: 2026-06-03.

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- This suggests tail latency is often a coordination problem spanning host+driver+NVLink rather than a single bad kernel.
- Avoid heavy Nsight captures for all runs — expensive. Fingerprint + selective deep-capture seems productive.
- Consider adding a lightweight per-callsite rolling histogram metric (in Prometheus) for instantiate->launch and launch->first-kernel to detect regressions automatically.

Attachments (placeholders):
- runA_qdstrm_excerpt.png (nsight timeline zoom around callsite marker)
- runA_nvlink.csv (small NVML sample)
- runA_cuda_event_timings.csv (per-callsite cudaEvent elapsed times)

End of note.

Unresolved: which mitigation (stream priority vs capture consolidation vs CPU isolation) will be least invasive with durable p95/p99 improvement. Keep experiments narrow and collect before/after with the same request mix.
